OWNER SQUAWKED AIRCRAFT WAS NOT PRODUCING ENOUGH RT RUDDER TRIM TO CENTER THE TURN COORDINATOR BALL.  THIS CONDITION WAS CORRECTED TWICE TO NO AVAIL BY POPPING THE INDICATOR PIN BACK INTO ITS GROOVE.  THE CONDITION WOULD RECUR DURING NEXT FLIGHT.  AFTER FURTHER INVESTIGATION, DISCOVERED RUDDER TRIM WHEEL HAD EXCESSIVE UP AND DOWN PLAY.  AS A RESULT, THE SPROCKET ON THE TRIM WHEEL THAT DRIVES THE AFT TRIM SPROCKET WOULD TEND TO SKIP CAUSING THE INDICATOR TO PREMATURELY REACH ITS STOP. WHEN FLAP FOLLOW-UP CABLE IS INSTALLED IN AIRCRAFT, IT HAS AN INTERNAL BIND WHICH CAUSES THE BELLCRANK IN THE LEFT WING TO 'JERK' AS THE MOTION OF THE BELLCRANK OVERCOMES THE BINDING OF THE CABLE.  THIS 'JERKING' CAUSES THE RIB TO WHICH THE BELLCRANK IS ATTACHED TO 'OIL CAN' A CONSIDERABLE AMOUNT.  THE FLAP INDICATOR ALSO 'JERKS' AND CAUSES AN AUDIBLE POPPING SOUND.  THE CABLE WORKS SMOOTH ON THE BENCH.  IF A 90 DEGREE BEND IS PUT ON THE CABLE (LESS THAN WHAT IT WOULD BE INSTALLED) THE CABLE BINDS.  A CESSNA TECH REP DID NOT HAVE A SOLUTION OTHER THAN TO 'TRY A DIFFERENT CABLE'.  THREE ADDITIONAL NEW CABLES WERE TRIED WITH THE SAME RESULTS.

AFTER ALLOWING ENGINE TO COOL SUFFICIENTLY, ENGINE START AND RUN-UP WERE NORMAL.

THE PILOT REPORTED THERE WAS AN ABNORMAL 'THUMP' NOISE COMING FROM THE NOSE GEAR AREA WHEN THE GEAR WAS RETRACTED ON SEVERAL OCCASIONS.  AN INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE CENTER RT NOSE LANDING GEAR DOOR BELLCRANK/HINGE WAS BROKEN IN HALF.  AN INSPECTION OF THE ENTIRE NOSE GEAR AND WHEELWELL AREA SHOWED NO FURTHER DAMAGE.  METAL FATIGUE IS THE SUSPECTED CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE.  SUBMITTER SUGGESTED CLOSE INSPECTION OF THESE HINGES BE MADE ANY TIME LANDING GEAR WORK IS PERFORMED AS WELL AS DURING ALL PRE AND POST-FLIGHT INSPECTIONS.

SUBMITTER STATED THE PROBLEM WAS VAPORIZATION OF FUEL DUE TO EXCESSIVE HEAT.  ENG ALLOWED TO COOL 3 HRS AND OPER CHK'D SATISFACTORY.  CESSNA NOTIFIED.

(CAN) ON TAKEOFF, THE LEFT INBOARD MAIN WHEEL ASSEMBLY SHED ITS ENTIRE TREAD.  ALTHOUGH THIS WAS A RECAPPED TIRE, THE TREAD DID NOT SEPARATE AT THE RECAP.   IN THIS CASE, THE RETREAD LAYER AND THE LAYER OF THE RUBBER FROM THE RETREAD TO THE FIRST LAYER OF CORD SEPARATED FROM THE REST OF THE TIRE.  THE TREAD DAMAGED THE GEAR DOOR AS IT CAME APART, BUT DID NOT CAUSE ENOUGH DAMAGE TO THE GEAR TO AFFECT ITS OPERATION.  THE AIRCRAFT LANDED WITHOUT INCIDENT, THE TIRE WAS CHANGED. THE TIRE REMAINED INFLATED EVEN THOUGH ITS TREAD WAS MISSING.

(CAN) THE AIRCRAFT WAS PARKED AND THE ENGINES SHUT DOWN, WHEN, WITH THE BATTERY STILL ON, THE CABIN FILLED WITH SMOKE. INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE FLAP MOTOR HAD OVERHEATED, SEIZED AND BEGAN TO SMOKE.  THE CAUSE WAS THE UPLIMIT SWITCH NOT MAKING CONTACT WHEN THE FLAPS WERE RETRACTED AFTER LANDING.  THIS KEPT POWER ON THE MOTOR WHICH WAS UNABLE TO ROTATE CAUSING IT TO OVERHEAT AND SMOKE.  THE FLAP MOTOR AND GEARBOX WERE REPLACED, THE UPLIMIT SWITCH ADJUSTED, FLAPS RIGGED, THE AIRCRAFT RETURNED TO SERVICE.

THE VALVE WAS REPLACED AND THE AIRCRAFT GROUND RUN WITH THE SYSTEM TESTING SERVICEABLE.
